analysis.title: BoJ Holds / Asia Stock Narrative / US Big Tech / KRW Vs. TWD
key_insights: BoJ held rates at 1.25% with an 8-1 vote. The statement reads modestly hawkish and supports a December hike as the base case. FY2027 core CPI forecast is 2.6% vs UBS Research at 2.5%. Front-end pricing still has three more hikes over the next 12 months.

BoJ documented an acceleration in ETF disposal (JPY330-860 bn annually, starting January 2027) and explicitly excluded the proposed food-tax cut from its inflation outlook. FY2027 growth forecast is 0.7%.

Asian tech earnings have generally been positive, but the regional stock narrative is driven by doubts over US hyperscaler cash flow growth and its ability to keep funding Asia tech's book to bill. UBS positioning data shows a substantial reduction in crowding across Asian tech.
KOSPI was down about 5% (up to 5.5% at one point) on Friday morning while Hong Kong was up about 1%. Foreigners sold $850 mn of Korean cash equities, $650 mn of it in tech.

Amazon Q3 AWS grew 39% y/y vs buyside bogeys of 44-45%, with AWS margin of 38.7% vs about 40% expected. Management pointed to AWS growth above 40% in both 2027 and 2028 and high-teens y/y advertising growth in Q4 2026. Buyside expectations for 2027-28 were already above 40%.

Intel is down 16% vs about 8.7% implied volatility. Q3 revenue was $16.5 bn and EPS $0.52 vs consensus of $16.58 bn and $0.41. Q4 guidance is $15-16 bn revenue and $0.25 EPS vs consensus of $17.14 bn and $0.44. Supply constraints limit server (Xeon) delivery, and PC weakness is expected to last through at least the first half of next year.

Alphabet feedback is the most negative since early 2025. Search growth was the most debated metric. Faster growth in lower-monetization AI Mode queries offset the highest search query growth in five years, and the desk sees this as a structural headwind. An Alphabet agent product may compete with Google's own economics.

US retail investors bought the dip for the sixth time this month, with UBS RMM flow at the 72nd percentile vs 3y. AI Software fell 3.0%, AI Semis 2.9% and AI Risk 2.6% on Thursday. Systematic selling included CTA selling in ES1 and NQ1 and $9 bn of leveraged ETP selling.
For Friday, ES1 has the most CTA sell triggers (5 within -2.5%) and RTY1 has the most buy triggers (3 within +2.5%).

AI sentiment affects KRW and TWD differently. AI strength brings USDTWD selling on equity inflows but USDKRW buying on equity hedging. AI weakness brings USDTWD buying on outflows and exporter supply in USDKRW. The desk watches a 1320-1350 USDKRW range, with exporter supply above 1340.
The CBC signaled that 32.50 in USDTWD is not a hard line in the sand, and systematic names have added USD longs over the past two sessions.
Iran received a letter from US Vice President Vance. Iran's Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf said its conditions have been clearly stated and the carrot-and-stick approach has no effect.
RBNZ's Hansen is '50-50' on a December hike after backing the unexpected OCR hold. UBS rates sales suggest selling AU 10y MMS vs buying NZ 10y MMS because the RBNZ may fall behind the curve.
Lagarde will leave the ECB on Feb. 7, 2027, ahead of her October term expiry. Klaas Knot and Pablo Hernandez de Cos are seen as frontrunners to succeed her. Markets showed little reaction.
ECB's Moulin said the ECB is taking a measured approach to inflation, with pressures largely imported.
Tokyo October core CPI was 2.6% y/y, in line with forecasts and down from 2.7% in September. Both measures remain above the BoJ's 2% target.

Australia Q3 final demand PPI rose 1.1% q/q vs 1.0% consensus (Q2: 1.3%), with annual inflation steady at 3.6%. Q3 trimmed mean CPI was 1.0% q/q and 3.7% y/y, and September headline CPI was 4.3% y/y. UBS sees a 25bp RBA hike to 4.85% in November as very likely, with market pricing at 80-90%.

FX flow monitor: hedge funds were net USD sellers in nine of the last 10 trading days, with 10-day flows below the 5th percentile of the past year. The USDBRL short unwind was a -5 sigma move on October 26, and USDBRL trades above 5.40.
UBS FX sales suggest being short IDR over a 3-6 month horizon via topside seagulls or a 1x2x1 call fly in USDIDR, on a weakening current account and slowing FDI.
The Bank of Canada hiked. UBS FX strategy sees USDCAD rebounding toward 1.42, while the FX desk suggests taking profit on USDCAD shorts around 1.40.
Egypt's central bank raised its rate by 100bp to 20%, its first hike since 2024, after the pound fell more than 7% in a month. The desk sees limited effect on spot direction.

US equity derivatives desk sees tech and AI weakness producing rotation into Value, Small Caps, Consumer and rate-sensitive cyclicals rather than risk-off. S&P vol is compressing, and GOOGL's roughly 12% decline vs about 5% implied did not generate aggressive downside demand.
USDKRW traded toward 1335 from 1340 early Friday, then consolidated back to about 1338. USDTWD 1m NDF trades at 32.620/720 after stops briefly drove it above 32.700.
AUD STIR desk prefers steepening Dec/Feb or Dec/Mar around 5.5bp and staying long the U7/M7 structure under the 'mullet' theme (short the front, long the back).
In SSAs, OATs widened about 6bp from the tights on ECB-driven volatility as real money sold 20y against 10y. Covered bonds were more resilient.

market_movers.rationale: Q3 AWS growth of 39% and margin of 38.7% missed buyside expectations of 44-45% and about 40%. Management pointed to AWS growth above 40% in 2027 and 2028.
Stock is down 16% on Q4 guidance of $15-16 bn revenue and $0.25 EPS vs consensus of $17.14 bn and $0.44, with supply constraints limiting server shipments.
Search missed the Street as faster growth in lower-monetization AI Mode queries offset record query growth. The desk calls this a structural headwind.

sector_views.rationale: Tech and AI weakness is driving rotation into Value, Small Caps, Consumer and rate-sensitive cyclicals rather than risk-off.
Flows favor Gold and Rails as clients trim higher-beta exposure.

earnings_insights: Amazon Q3 2026 (reported): AWS grew 39% y/y vs buyside expectations of about 44-45%. AWS margin was 38.7% vs about 40% expected. Management pointed to high-teens y/y advertising growth in Q4 2026 and AWS growth above 40% in 2027 and 2028.

Intel Q3 2026 (reported): revenue $16.5 bn vs consensus $16.58 bn, EPS $0.52 vs consensus $0.41. Intel Foundry revenue $6.7 bn vs $6.05 bn expected, Client Computing $7.3 bn vs $8.95 bn expected. Gross margin 44% vs 42% expected, operating margin 19.6% vs 16.1% expected. Q4 guidance (company): revenue $15-16 bn and EPS $0.25 vs consensus $17.14 bn and $0.44.

Alphabet Q3 2026 (reported): search came in slightly below Street expectations despite the highest search query growth in five years, as faster growth in lower-monetization AI Mode queries offset it. The company flagged one-time headwinds on the call. Shares fell about 12-14% vs about 5% implied.
Microsoft and Alphabet post-close earnings on Thursday triggered selling in AI names. Asia technology earnings have generally been positive, with some exceptions.

The BoJ's forecast is above UBS Research's 2.5%.

In line with forecasts, down from 2.7% in September. Keeps further BoJ hikes in view.

trade_ideas.description: Sell AU 10y MMS vs buy NZ 10y MMS
trade_ideas.rationale: The RBNZ hold raises the risk that it falls behind the curve if inflation persists, and the Kiwi swap curve has not steepened enough to reflect that. Australia looks different.

trade_ideas.description: Short IDR via USDIDR topside seagulls or a 1x2x1 call fly
trade_ideas.rationale: The current account balance may erode further with slowing FDI, and the external environment is difficult. USDIDR is a candidate for a sustained grind higher.

trade_ideas.description: Steepen AUD STIR Dec/Feb or Dec/Mar around 5.5bp, and stay long U7/M7 while shifting some shorts into M7
trade_ideas.rationale: The desk sees interest in Nov/Dec steepeners as protection if the RBA follows the RBNZ and waits until December, and likes the 'mullet' theme (short the front, long the back).

trade_ideas.description: Take profit on USDCAD shorts around 1.40
trade_ideas.rationale: Momentum is slowing, and UBS FX strategy sees USDCAD rebounding toward 1.42.
trade_ideas.risk: Sustained BoC hiking cycle, which the FX desk says is far from certain.

risk_factors: Doubts over US hyperscaler cash flow growth and their ability to fund Asia tech's book to bill.
Crowded positioning in AI and hyperscalers, with demanding earnings expectations.
Intel supply constraints and a PC slowdown lasting through at least the first half of next year.
Structural pressure on Alphabet search economics from lower-monetization AI Mode queries and a possible competing agent product.
Systematic selling by CTAs and leveraged ETPs adds to downside moves in US equity futures.
Further erosion of Indonesia's current account balance with slowing FDI.
Imported inflation and regional conflict pressure on Egypt's pound.
RBNZ falling behind the curve if inflation pressures persist.
vol_and_positioning: S&P vol continues to compress, with SPX call-spread demand and VIX put-spread buying pointing to upside participation and vol fading.

GOOGL's roughly 12% decline vs about 5% implied failed to generate aggressive downside demand, with longer-dated put selling dominating flows. Tech protection is being unwound through MAGS hedges, and MSFT overwrite supply persists.
Intel is down 16% vs about 8.7% implied volatility.
UBS positioning data suggests a substantial reduction in crowding across Asian tech.
Retail dip-buying (UBS RMM flow at the 72nd percentile vs 3y) is the sixth buy-the-dip this month. Post-FOMC excess buy flow was +$2 bn.
CTAs sold ES1 and NQ1 (one trigger each) and crossed three buy triggers in RTY1. $9 bn of leveraged ETP selling triggered late-day selling.
Long-only funds are trimming crowded winners, while hedge funds moved from early selling to net buying as covering added fuel to under-owned exposures.
Hedge funds were net USD sellers in nine of the last 10 days, with 10-day flows below the 5th percentile vs the past year.
USDBRL short unwind was a -5 sigma move on October 26, and YTD cumulative longs were reduced by more than one-third.
USDIDR vol has not realized well and the RR/ATM ratio has been repricing higher.
Korean forwards: 1s -92, IMM -310, 1s12s -1310. Taiwan forwards: 1s -10, IMM -25, 1s12s -80.
geopolitical: Iran received a letter from US Vice President JD Vance addressed to its top security official Mohsen Rezaee. Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf said Iran's conditions have been stated to the mediators and the carrot-and-stick approach has no effect.
President Trump said he authorized Vance to contact Tehran, with the letter meant to assist Iran with medical supplies.
Lagarde will leave the ECB early on Feb. 7, 2027, giving EU leaders time to choose a successor before France's presidential election. Marine Le Pen's National Rally criticised the move.
The Israel election was the most notable development in CEEMEA flows, and asset managers began fading the move in USDILS.
Regional conflict and elevated energy prices are weighing on Egypt's current account and the pound.

tension_points.bull_case: AI is being repriced against demanding earnings expectations rather than abandoned. Asia tech earnings have been generally positive, and Amazon pointed to AWS growth above 40% in 2027 and 2028. Rotation into Value, Small Caps and Consumer is constructive and vol is compressing.
tension_points.bear_case: Doubts over US hyperscaler cash flow growth and funding of Asia tech's book to bill drove KOSPI down 5%. Amazon's AWS missed, Alphabet's search faces a structural mix headwind, and Intel guided sharply lower.
tension_points.what_invalidates: AMZN's call failing to bridge the Q3 AWS miss and the longer-term growth confidence.
